*Update 12.05.2025*

* We concluded the [measurement of Amsterdam Schiphol Airport branding|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MP/pages/6255706200/NL+-+Amsterdam+Schiphol+Airport+Branding+OOH+-+April+2025] for the measurement period 31.03 - 30.4.

*MAIN CONCLUSIONS*

* FTRs could not be measured as we couldn’t find a stable relationship of “to airport” and “from airport” FTRs before the branding period to take make a reliable measurement of impact.
* All Rides were shown to be positively affected by the intervention, generating 208 incremental rides daily (32% of total from airport rides) with an ASP of €40.5.
* The branding generated an average incr. ROI (= incr. GMV/Cost) of 18.2 during the measurement period.
* The results might be positively influenced by tourists in Amsterdam during the tulip season. The "actual" iROI of the branding in a different period could therefore be significantly lower.
* Although we could not measure the impact of the branding on First Time Rides, there’s a visible uplift in the number of arrival rides (from airport), most probably due to incoming tourists. Typically, we attribute 1Y LTV to FTRs to account for potential future rides. So, in theory, we could generate considerably more GMV from these users in subsequent rides, which isn't reflected in this ROI measurement.

Results of the post-analysis (data till 6th May). Details in this [sheet| https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1TQ1qYC1CTrzrPB3CsyGA5HwPjZBtzxUCiEhOIquUct8/edit?gid=2118302605#gid=2118302605].

+*Primary Metric: Conversion rate*+

* Conversion was defined as a user placing at least one order during the experiment period.
* Results were analyzed using a one-sided hypothesis test with 95% confidence.

*Conclusion:* There is no statistically significant difference in conversion rates between treatment and control groups in any market. This aligns with our hypothesis that stopping marketing emails to inactive users does not negatively affect the rides.

+*Analysis of Guardrail Metrics (Rides/GMV)*+
Across all three countries, treatment groups showed stable or slightly improved performance across rides taken, GMV, and engagement per user:

* No negative impact was observed on # of rides taken and GMV.
* Rides per user and GMV per user remained comparable between test and control.
* GMV per ride saw minimal change (mostly within ±1%).

*Conclusion:* Secondary business metrics remained healthy, further reinforcing that discontinuing emails to inactive users has no adverse effects on the business.

Looking at the bigger picture: *we are not a party to the franchise agreement*, which means we are *not obligated* to prove or disprove any connection between the former franchisee (Mr. Širilla) and Mantid s.r.o. That responsibility lies solely with the franchisor and franchisee. That said, we can break this down into two possible scenarios:

# +We suspect, but cannot confirm, a connection:+
In this case, I’d recommend informing the franchisor that we are aware of the potential link, but currently have no definitive proof. We can politely explain that since we are not a party to the agreement, our role is limited, and there is a possibility that Mantid s.r.o. is genuinely independent. Therefore, it is up to the franchisor to prove the connection. If such proof is provided, we’re happy to take further action — including limiting visibility of the related listings.
# +We have clear evidence of a connection:+
In this scenario, the previous guidance applies — we should not allow listings under a different company that appears to be a workaround of a valid non-compete clause.

*Update 12/05*

After reviewing the lifecycle stage definitions, we found that these definitions are quite complex and not mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive (MECE). For example, a user can belong to growth - frequency and churn - loyal stages at the same time. This led to difficulty in mapping out the lifecycle stage logic in SQL. 

Worked on re-defining the lifecycle stages that are similar to the ones proposed before but are MECE:

* *New:* 0 lifetime rides AND signed up <= 90 days ago.
* *Never Active:* 0 lifetime rides AND signed up > 90 days ago
* *Activated:* 1 lifetime ride AND last ride <= 45 days ago.
* *Growth - Upsell:* 2-4 lifetime rides AND last ride <= 45 days ago.
* *Growth - Engaged:* >=5 lifetime rides AND last ride <= 45 days ago.
* *At Risk:* >=1 lifetime ride AND last ride between 46-90 days ago.
* *Churned:* >=1 lifetime ride AND last ride > 90 days ago.

These definitions are still a work in progress and will need to be discussed with the team before finalization.

Results of the experiment post-analysis (data till 6th May). Details in this [sheet|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1TQ1qYC1CTrzrPB3CsyGA5HwPjZBtzxUCiEhOIquUct8/edit?gid=2118302605#gid=2118302605].

+*Primary Metric: Conversion rate*+

* Conversion was defined as a user placing at least one order during the experiment period.
* Results were analyzed using a one-sided hypothesis test with 95% confidence.

*Conclusion:* There is no statistically significant difference in conversion rates between treatment and control groups in any market. This aligns with our hypothesis that stopping marketing emails to inactive users does not negatively affect the rides.

+*Analysis of Guardrail Metrics (Rides/GMV)*+
Across all three countries, treatment groups showed stable or slightly improved performance across rides taken, GMV, and engagement per user:

* No negative impact was observed on # of rides taken and GMV.
* Rides per user and GMV per user remained comparable between test and control.
* GMV per ride saw minimal change (mostly within ±1%).

*Conclusion:* Secondary business metrics remained healthy, further reinforcing that discontinuing emails to inactive users has no adverse effects on the business.

+*Next Steps*+

* Deliverability Impact: To be measured by Dovainis
* Automation for Roll-out: If we proceed with a wider roll-out, we'll need to automate updating the {{is_email_sunset}} attribute to Braze.

We had to migrate away from DB publisher (for publishing of payment update and payment status update events) when migrating from MySQL to TiDB. The DB publisher was configured to publish events as-soon-as-possible as they were part of customer facing flows - ie. DB publisher was polling very often in short intervals, high amount of events and TiDB “garbage collection” when deleted records still stay (soft deleted, invisible) in DBs for some time until physically deleted, but they are still part of DB space - those caused that queries on what looked like empty tables took sometimes seconds, causing neighborood issues to other queries and even DBs on the same cluster.

Response from PINT/SREs/DBREs pretty much was that to try to achieve “near-time” events publishing through DB is pretty much non-sense, and we should go for a different mechanism.

Hence we implemented direct publishing with DB fallback. ie. we publish directly and only when-and-if the direct publishing fails then we write to DB and then publish from DB. Practically all events are published directly, the DB fallback is virtually never used (in fact).

ie. the super-high DB load caused by DB publisher is gone, no problems with slow-queries there anymore.

….

TL;DR: if “once-in-a-while” publishing of events is OK, then right approach still might be to tune DB publisher, if high-volume “near-time” publishing of events is required then go away from DB publisher.

The DB fallback for direct publisher was implemented by [~accountid:6001a70dd364960139286b71] - he can share additional details if required.

After reviewing the lifecycle stage definitions, we found that these definitions are quite complex and not mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive (MECE). For example, a user can belong to growth - frequency and churn - loyal stages at the same time. This led to difficulty in mapping out the lifecycle stage logic in SQL. 

Worked on re-defining the lifecycle stages that are similar to the ones proposed before but are MECE:

* *New:* 0 lifetime rides AND signed up <= 90 days ago.
* *Never Active:* 0 lifetime rides AND signed up > 90 days ago
* *Activated:* 1 lifetime ride AND last ride <= 45 days ago.
* *Growth - Upsell:* 2-4 lifetime rides AND last ride <= 45 days ago.
* *Growth - Engaged:* >=5 lifetime rides AND last ride <= 45 days ago.
* *At Risk:* >=1 lifetime ride AND last ride between 46-90 days ago.
* *Churned:* >=1 lifetime ride AND last ride > 90 days ago.

These definitions are still a work in progress and will need to be discussed with the team before finalization.

Verbal claims like _“I heard from someone”_ etc are not reliable enough for us to act. Hi [~accountid:6298a958658d580068899aa3], unfortunately the attached document does not solve the issue. The attached PoA authorizes Anna Pawliczek to sign the lease agreement on behalf of Still Water sp. z o.o - it does not relate to the problem of invalidity of the lending agreement. I will try to explain again:

* We, Bolt, need to sign the lease agreement either with *the owner* of the real estate or with the *entity who holds a valid legal title* to use the real estate and to lease it to other entities;
* the owner is Sebastian Goliszewski. As we see from the attached lending agreement (umowa użyczenia), his intention was to lend the real estate to Still Water sp. z o.o, so that this company could lease the real estate;
* however, the attached lending agreement is invalid by the virtue of law due to the reasons previously explained by me. Consequently, at the moment, Still Water cannot lease the real estate to us, because it does not validly hold the real estate.
* in this situation, we can take two possible actions:
** sign the lease agreement with Sebastian Goliszewski who is the owner of the real estate; or
** if we want to sign the agreement with Still Water sp. z o.o., Sebastian Goliszewski must validly sign the lending agreement.
* To cure the situation, Sebastian Goliszewski must do the following actions:
** take up the shareholder’s meeting resolution, pursuant to art. 210 of CCC, to appoint an attorney to sign the lending agreement on behalf of the company with Sebastian Goliszewski;
** then, the appointed person, must sign the lending agreement on behalf of the company with Sebastian Goliszewski - only then the agreement would be valid and we could sign the lease agreement with Still Water.

Regards, Piotr

Hello team,As previously discussed, we’re preparing to kick off the license requirements mapping exercise with the Public Policy team.The first phase shall focus on conducting a risk assessment to identify which licenses carry the most significant impact, but we already have some relevant data available in the following sources:

* *France – Registration (Regulated, no license required)*
* *Poland – Taxi Services Intermediation License*
* *Romania – Platform License*
* *Thailand – Operating License*
* South Africa – Unregulated
** _In ZA, ride-hailing drivers are required to obtain operating licenses, though enforcement has been inconsistent._
* _UK – 58 Operating Licenses_
** _Already mapped_ [_here_|https://www.cognitoforms.com/bolttechnologyo%C3%BC/compliancerequirementdatabase/entries/2-all-entries]

** _New market, no GMV indication, but it’s in the Public Policy - 2025 Reporting/Budgeting document)_

Hi [~accountid:5acb1f48d8b95a2b34f150a8] 

I hope you are well. As per Anusha’s comment, I have been looking into this claim and have been preparing for the mediation. 

Key points to note are as follows: 

* *Mediation details:* the mediation will be a telephone mediation and is set for 14 May 2025 from 10:00 to 12:00. Anusha and I will attend the mediation. 
* *Recommendations:* +we ultimately recommend offering the claimant a higher settlement amount on the basis that it will be cheaper and quicker to settle than to defend this claim in court (please see our reasoning set out below).+ In summary, the claimant is claiming the total sum of *£187.01*, a breakdown of which is set out below: 

(a) journey with Bolt: £47.60

(b) onward journey with Uber: £18.96

(c) compensation (which we will argue against): £50 

(d) claim form fee: £35 (which, for some reason is claimed twice and we will argue against)

(e) interest: £0.45

To date, we have offered a partial refund of £19.60 and then a full refund of the fare (£47.60) which was not acknowledged or accepted by the claimant. 

As mentioned above, we recommend offering a higher settlement amount. Mediation provides a lower-cost, lower-risk opportunity to resolve the dispute amicably. +*Please can you confirm the maximum amount you are willing to offer in mediation (if you are willing to offer a settlement amount).*+

 

+*Reasons for offering a higher settlement amount*+ 

# *Risk:* if helpful, we have set out below a brief summary of our defence position which we will set out in the mediation. Although our assessment is that Bolt has a +*moderate to strong*+ defence if this case was to proceed to court and an +*estimated likelihood success of 55% - 60%*+, the risks of this case not settling and proceeding to the small claims court are as follows: 
# *Defending the case in court will incur costs (legal resource) and time:* we estimate that the total time spent in preparing for and attending a court hearing would be approximately 12-20 hours, and approximately £1,200-£2,000 plus VAT for external counsel support (advice and appearance at court).  
# *Potential reputational risk or precedent setting:* if the case was to proceed to court and the claimant was to win the case against Bolt, there is a strong risk of reputational damage (i.e. negative publicity against Bolt) and a precedent being set of a claimant winning a case against Bolt (the risk being that more passengers will submit claims against Bolt on the basis that this claim was successful). 
# *Weaknesses in our defence:* that the claimant will argue against all of the above points and UK Consumer Law typically favours the consumer in claims and disputes. Although our defence is strong (a summary of our defence is set out below if helpful), it is not 100% watertight and this is because (1) the platform did malfunction to some extent as, although the claimant updated the drop-off location on the platform (and this was confirmed by customer service), the updated drop-off location was not updating on the driver’s system and (2) the customer service was not optimal.  

+*Bolt’s defence*+ 

Bolt has a relatively strong defence and the points that we will be arguing in the mediation are as follows: 

# the claimant entered the incorrect destination for the journey; 
# although the claimant may argue that there was a technical error on the platform, our terms and conditions for passengers clearly states (clause 8(b)) that Bolt is not liable for any errors in the provision or function of the Bolt platform.  
# although the claimant alleges that he exited the vehicle due to “concerns about [his] safety”, a review of the recorded telephone conversation confirms that safety was never raised as a concern (the claimant sounded relaxed and clearly reassures the driver that the issues from the journey were not the driver’s fault). 
# The claimant exited the vehicle voluntarily (and this is also verified in the recorded telephone conversation) and, although the claimant is seeking compensation for the onward Uber travel (£18.96), our terms and conditions are clear that Bolt is not liable for any onward travel costs incurred.  

As above, please confirm the maximum settlement amount you are willing to offer and we will put this forward in the mediation. Of course, if you do not want to offer a settlement amount, we will work with this position. I would be very happy to have a quick call with you to discuss if helpful 🙂 . 

Thank you!

Hi [~accountid:712020:da3fd2a6-2c47-4a89-98da-78c26d3c9b96] Can you please update me on the status here?

As a brief test of predictive power, we fit a log-log linear regression for each city (across 6 folds over time, each with 52 weeks - one year - of training data and 8 weeks - two months - for testing) using only active riders as the predictor (without removing seasonality). 

* Average MAPE (avg): 12.7%
* Median MAPE (avg): 11.3%
* Minimum MAPE (avg): 6.0%
* Maximum MAPE (avg): 24.7%
* Cities with Lowest MAPE: Tallinn (6.3%), Bangkok (6.3%), Nairobi (7.3%), Vilnius (7.9%) and Kyiv (8.9%)
* Cities with Highest MAPE: Valletta (29.0%), Phuket (27.3%), Oslo (20.0%), Zagreb (18.3%), Stockholm (18.0%)

The result is not very good, however we need to keep in mind that without modeling seasonality properly we might lose a lot of accuracy. Results of these models, as well as overall correlation between the metrics (sessions and active riders) are presented in [this spreadsheet|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/13IqwLrFcIEfURN6bYfPsKBn5YomU-U055bgjmhRaowo/edit?usp=sharing].

+*BACKGROUND*+

* A FO (I cannot access the profile) has asked if we can provide more information to theFO regarding their driver’s average trip ratings (which he can already view through the fleet portal). In particular, FO wants to know if he can be provided with:
** (i) A percentage of trips that received a 1-star rating and 2-star rating (as a percentage of total trips); and
** (ii) A ‘summary of the relevant rider comments that were provided to the driver' - i.e., paraphrasing.

+*ANALYSIS*+

* We do not provide ratings / comments linking to specific trips, as this poses a risk to the rights and freedoms of passengers.
* However, provided that rating / comments cannot be linked to specific trips, the risk profile is lowered. As such, percentages and paraphrasing could be ok.
** Worth asking if FOs are generally notified about safety complaints, or whether there is a reason to *_not_* notify them of the same.
** Would also be useful to see an example of what providing this would look like.
* Nevertheless, we are wading into tricky waters here re monitoring driver performance based on ratings. Admittedly, it would be the FO acting on this feedback, but still.
* In terms of our basis for doing so:
** *Purpose*: To monitor driver performance from a safety perspective.
** *Legal* *basis*: Legitimate interest (interest in ensuring drivers meet safety standards).
** *Transparency*: Not specifically covered in updated Driver Privacy Notice. This is main compliance risk.
* +*Conclusion*+:
** Preference would be not to do this. It is currently outside of the expectation of drivers, and is not currently covered in our privacy language. As such, doing so creates risk.
** If we absolutely HAVE to do this, then preference would be to provide it as high level as possible.

* *In short:* The preference would be to +*not*+ share this data (i.e., percentages of trips that received 1-star and 2-star ratings, and a summary of the relevant rider comments) with the Fleet Owner. This is because:
** Such data sharing is not currently covered in our driver privacy notice, and would be outside of the usual expectations of fleet drivers. If one of the fleet drivers found out about this sharing and was not happy about it, they could raise a legitimate privacy complaint with Bolt.
** Any cases of data sharing for the purpose of monitoring driver performance (even though it is the FO that is ultimately making the final decisions here) may get us into tricky waters with regards to reclassification.
** My understanding is that this case involves a single FO asking if they can have this information as a ‘nice to have’ rather than as the result of a pressing need.
* If there was a _pressing need_ to share this data (in which case let me know), we could consider sharing this data as a one-off, but I would need to see what the final export looked like so that we can take any steps as needed to de-risk the data that we are sending.



In order to make a final decision on this, I therefore need the following - please could you source these?

* Confirmation of _why exactly_ the FO needs this data (i.e., is it urgent or just a nice to have)?
* Confirmation of what information the FO already has access to with regards to safety complaints and other types of negative rider feedback.

Hi [~accountid:5acb1f48d8b95a2b34f150a8]

I hope you are well. As per Anusha’s comment, I have been looking into this claim and have been preparing for the mediation. 

Key points to note are as follows: 

* *Mediation details:* the mediation will be a telephone mediation and is set for 14 May 2025 from 10:00 to 12:00. Anusha and I will attend the mediation. 
* *Recommendations:* +we ultimately recommend offering the claimant a higher settlement amount on the basis that it will be cheaper and quicker to settle than to defend this claim in court (please see our reasoning set out below).+ In summary, the claimant is claiming the total sum of *£187.01*, a breakdown of which is set out below:

(a) journey with Bolt: £47.60

(b) onward journey with Uber: £18.96

(c) compensation (which we will argue against): £50 

(d) claim form fee: £35 (which, for some reason is claimed twice and we will argue against)

(e) interest: £0.45

To date, we have offered a partial refund of £19.60 and then a full refund of the fare (£47.60) which was not acknowledged or accepted by the claimant. 

As mentioned above, we recommend offering a higher settlement amount. Mediation provides a lower-cost, lower-risk opportunity to resolve the dispute amicably. +*Please can you confirm the maximum amount you are willing to offer in mediation (if you are willing to offer a settlement amount).*+

 

+*Reasons for offering a higher settlement amount*+ 

# *Risk:* if helpful, we have set out below a brief summary of our defence position which we will set out in the mediation. Although our assessment is that Bolt has a +*moderate to strong*+ defence if this case was to proceed to court and an +*estimated likelihood success of 55% - 60%*+, the risks of this case not settling and proceeding to the small claims court are as follows: 
# *Defending the case in court will incur costs (legal resource) and time:* we estimate that the total time spent in preparing for and attending a court hearing would be approximately 12-20 hours, and approximately £1,200-£2,000 plus VAT for external counsel support (advice and appearance at court).  
# *Potential reputational risk or precedent setting:* if the case was to proceed to court and the claimant was to win the case against Bolt, there is a strong risk of reputational damage (i.e. negative publicity against Bolt) and a precedent being set of a claimant winning a case against Bolt (the risk being that more passengers will submit claims against Bolt on the basis that this claim was successful). 
# *Weaknesses in our defence:* that the claimant will argue against all of the above points and UK Consumer Law typically favours the consumer in claims and disputes. Although our defence is strong (a summary of our defence is set out below if helpful), it is not 100% watertight and this is because (1) the platform did malfunction to some extent as, although the claimant updated the drop-off location on the platform (and this was confirmed by customer service), the updated drop-off location was not updating on the driver’s system and (2) the customer service was not optimal.  

+*Bolt’s defence*+

Bolt has a relatively strong defence and the points that we will be arguing in the mediation are as follows: 

# the claimant entered the incorrect destination for the journey; 
# although the claimant may argue that there was a technical error on the platform, our terms and conditions for passengers clearly states (clause 8(b)) that Bolt is not liable for any errors in the provision or function of the Bolt platform.  
# although the claimant alleges that he exited the vehicle due to “concerns about [his] safety”, a review of the recorded telephone conversation confirms that safety was never raised as a concern (the claimant sounded relaxed and clearly reassures the driver that the issues from the journey were not the driver’s fault). 
# The claimant exited the vehicle voluntarily (and this is also verified in the recorded telephone conversation) and, although the claimant is seeking compensation for the onward Uber travel (£18.96), our terms and conditions are clear that Bolt is not liable for any onward travel costs incurred.  

As above, please confirm the maximum settlement amount you are willing to offer and we will put this forward in the mediation. Of course, if you do not want to offer a settlement amount, we will work with this position. I would be very happy to have a quick call with you to discuss if helpful 🙂 .

Thank you!

{code:sql}select delivery_vertical,
round(sum(potential_fraud_loss_eur)) as potential, 
round(sum(reporting_fraud_loss_eur)) as reporting,
count(distinct order_id) as count_orders,
count(distinct case when potential_fraud_loss_eur > 0 then order_id else null end) as count_potential,
round(count(distinct case when potential_fraud_loss_eur > 0 then order_id else null end) / count(distinct order_id), 4) as problem_order_rate,
round(sum(chargeback)) as chargeback, 
round(sum(failed)) as failed,
round(sum(user_price_eur)) as user_price,
round(avg(user_price_eur)) as avg_user_price,
round(sum(partner_price_eur)) as gmv,
round(sum(potential_fraud_loss_eur)/sum(partner_price_eur), 4) as potential_to_gmv,
round(sum(reporting_fraud_loss_eur)/sum(partner_price_eur), 4) as reporting_to_gmv,
round(sum(potential_fraud_loss_eur)/sum(user_price_eur), 4) as potential_to_user,
round(sum(reporting_fraud_loss_eur)/sum(user_price_eur), 4) as reporting_to_user,
round(sum(chargeback)/sum(partner_price_eur), 4) as chargeback_to_gmv,
round(sum(failed)/sum(partner_price_eur), 4) as failed_to_gmv,
round(sum(chargeback)/sum(user_price_eur), 4) as chargeback_to_user,
round(sum(failed)/sum(user_price_eur), 4) as failed_to_user
from(
select etl.created_date, etl.order_id, etl.potential_fraud_loss_eur, etl.reporting_fraud_loss_eur, etl.user_price_eur, etl.partner_price_eur, etl.current_chargeback_amount/etl.eur_currency_rate as chargeback, 
etl.current_failed_payment_amount/etl.eur_currency_rate as failed,
delivery_vertical 
from ng_public_spark.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders as etl
left join ng_delivery_spark.dim_order_delivery as fod

  and order_created_date between dateadd(current_date, -150) and dateadd(current_date, -90)   
where etl.order_type = 'food_delivery'
  and etl.created_date between date_add(current_date, -150) and dateadd(current_date, -90)
)
group by 1{code}

Hi All

Just a quick update following our call this morning with Liverpool City Council regarding the legal proceedings issued by Lime. The purpose of the call was to understand the Council’s position and how they plan to respond. Key points below:*_Liverpool City Council's Legal Position_*

* The Council is still considering whether to apply for an interim order to lift the automatic suspension. While this would allow the contract with Bolt to proceed, they acknowledged the financial risk and the possibility that the court may reject the application. They expect to make a decision later this week.
* The Council has not yet engaged external legal counsel and is relying on its in-house legal team to assess the claim. They’re still reviewing Lime’s arguments. While the Council cannot share the legal advice they’ve received so far (as it is privileged), they indicated that the advice does not confirm a definitive position in their favour.
* Lime has requested access to Bolt’s bid and the council's scoring. The Council is proposing a confidentiality ring so that only legal teams would have access. They believe Lime may have misunderstood parts of Bolt’s submission, and that clarification could lead to narrowing down this claim. The Council asked whether Bolt would consent to certain parts of our submission being disclosed to Lime under confidentiality terms.
* The council is keen to avoid a formal disclosure hearing (scheduled for June), which would be costly and time-consuming.
* The Council also mentioned they may explore Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR), a process to settle disputes without going to court.
* While the Council didn’t confirm whether they will continue with the incumbent operator during this period, they did mention they are looking into it, as they need to keep the government scheme running.

*_Timelines & TUPE_*

* If the suspension is lifted, the Council will coordinate with us to ensure sufficient time for TUPE consultation and planning. [@karolina.tadych|https://taxify.slack.com/team/U05EN2GV79D]

*_Takeaways from the Call_*

* Based on the discussion, it appears the Council is hesitant about applying for an interim order, the cost and risk associated with the application and the uncertainty of a favourable outcome seem to be key factors. While they haven’t ruled it out, their comments suggest they are leaning against this option. They’ve committed to updating Bolt later this week.
* That said, the Council does not appear inclined to abandon the tender process and may be exploring ADR as indicated by their head of legal. This suggests they may prefer a negotiated resolution over prolonged litigation.

*_Next Steps_*

* The Council has asked for confirmation of Bolt’s position - whether we intend to remain as an interested party or formally join the proceedings. Legal team has advised that our recommendation is to remain as an interested party, though I understand, [@haya.douidri|https://taxify.slack.com/team/U060TR0BJUS] you’d like me to clarify one final point with external counsel before deciding how you’d like to proceed.
* [@haya.douidri|https://taxify.slack.com/team/U060TR0BJUS] and [@giulio.delbalzo|https://taxify.slack.com/team/U07A3J6DKGW], you both indicated you’ll be reviewing the tender submission and will let the Council know by EOD tomorrow which parts you’re comfortable sharing with Lime (to help clarify any misunderstandings) and what should remain confidential.

Apparently, there is this court case which, in summary, says that a bicycle rental company is obligated to provide the name and address of the last renter if their bike was involved in a damaging incident. This duty applies even if the renter's identity is unknown to the victim, as long as the rental company can easily access the information. The company must provide this data when the accident has been sufficiently documented, such as through a police report or witness testimony. Moreover, apparently there is no requirement for formal documents from the police or court to trigger the disclosure, as long as the connection between the bike and the damage is clear.

Having taken a quick look at this particular case, I note the following:

* A rider, And Mi (“*User A*”) is claiming that their [+account+|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/identity/consumers/rider/117029482/overview] (“*Account 1*”) was ‘hacked’ on the basis that they have been charged from trips that they do not recognise.
* User A has complained about various charges made in May. If we look at User A’s order history, only 1 trip was taken in May (on 1 May, costing EUR 13.00). This does not match the screenshots provided by User A, which suggests that *the trips were taken via another account*.
* This has been confirmed by CS on the Beehive thread - the trips in question were taken via [+this account+|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/identity/consumers/rider/262189005/overview] (“*Account 2*”) by a rider called Juno Tero (“*User B*”).
* Both Account 1 and Account 2 have the same payment method on them (i.e., a visa card ending in 4269 - the “*Payment Method*”). We can assume that, because: (i) User A receives phone notifications regarding the Payment Method; (ii) User A is the one issuing this complaint; and (iii) Account 2 was only created very recently (it looks like this month), User A is the owner of the card. This suggests that *User B has somehow got hold of User A’s Payment Method, and is using it to take trips*.

Here’s what this means for us:

* This does not look like a data breach on the Bolt side. User B has independently gained access to User A’s Payment Method and is using it to fraudulently take trips. User A is being notified independently due to the charges to their card (it does not look like the charge notifications are coming from Bolt). None of this appears to be the result of a breach of security on the Bolt side (in particular, no account has been hacked here).

What we need to do (I would be grateful if you could push this forward):

* As a first step, check with [https://bolt.enterprise.slack.com/archives/C06R63EQ6CS|https://bolt.enterprise.slack.com/archives/C06R63EQ6CS|smart-link] whether they agree with this assessment and that no account compromise has occurred.
* If the channel concludes that this explanation is correct, we should notify User A to block their card on the grounds that someone else appears to have access to it. In the same message, we should explain to User A that their account has not been hacked.
* Then, we should loop into the Fraud Team to investigate User B’s actions and see if we have any grounds for taking action against User B (i.e., blocking Account 2).
* Once the above is done, the ticket can be closed. We do not need to notify the ODPO Team about this, since technically it is not s data breach.

Lēmums šajā lietā ir izdots attiecībā uz atbildīgo personu -  *OkoRide Latvija*. Tādēļ *visi paskaidrojumi un ar lietu saistītie dokumenti ir jāiesniedz autoparkam (ne mums)*, ne vēlāk kā 1 darba dienu pirms lietas izskatīšanas. Ja lietas izskatīšana notiek 2024. gada 15. maijā plkst. 10:45, dokumenti jāiesniedz līdz *14. maija plkst. 10:45.*

Tāpat ieteicams, lai autoparka pilnvarotie pārstāvji piedalās lietas izskatīšanā.


*Pārkāpums*
MK noteikumu Nr. 389 15. punkts nosaka:
_"Informāciju par tīmekļvietnes vai mobilās lietotnes pakalpojuma sniedzēju un pārvadātāju izvieto ārpusē uz autotransporta līdzekļa abām priekšējām durvīm (neizmantojot durvju stikloto daļu)."_

*Konstatētie pārkāpumi pēc Kontroles dienesta ziņojuma:*

# Uz abām priekšējām durvīm *nav iespējams nolasīt* informāciju par pārvadātāju.
# Uz transportlīdzekļa labajām durvīm *nav norādīta* tīmekļvietnes vai mobilās lietotnes pakalpojuma informācija.

h3. 1. Pārkāpums - "uz abām priekšējām durvīm nav iespējams nolasīt informāciju par pārvadātāju "

Es tiešām neredzu šādu info un durvīm. Tāpēc iesaku autoparkam sekojošu:

* Ja informācijas uz durvīm tiešām nav, *ieteicams to* paskaidrojumos *atzīt un nožēlot pārkāpumu*, atsaucoties uz Administratīvās atbildības likuma 20. panta pirmās daļas 1. punktu, kas paredz, ka atbildību *mīkstina apstāklis*, ja persona atzinusi un nožēlojusi izdarīto.
*  saskaņā ar Administratīvās atbildības likuma 20. panta otro daļu, var minēt arī “citus mīkstinošus apstākļus” –  te var rakstīt jebko, lai autoparks padomā kādu objektīvu pamatojumu, kādēļ prasība netika izpildīta. Var arī norādīt, ka pārkāpums nav radījis kaitējumu nevienai personai. 
* norādīt, kādi pasākumi veikti, lai pārkāpumu novērstu, piemēram, norādīt, ka attiecīgais transportlīdzeklis jau ir (minēt kad) nodots sadarbības partnerim, lai uz durvīm tiktu uzlīmēta pārvadātāja informācija. Norādīt, kas darīts, lai līdzīgi pārkāpumi neatkārtotos. 
* norādīt, ka lietā nav saskatāmi atbildību pastiprinošie apstākļi (Administratīvās atbildības likuma 21. pants)

*Šis pārkāpums nav saistīts ar Bolt zīmolvedības politika, tāpēc pamatojums jāsagatavo pašam autoparkam, ne mums.* 

h3. 2. Pārkāpums – "uz labajām durvīm nav norādīta tīmekļvietnes vai mobilās lietotnes pakalpojuma informācija."

Iesaku autoparkam šim apgalvojumam *nepiekrist*, jo:

* Saskaņā ar *MK noteikumu Nr. 389 anotāciju*, kura precizē noteikumu prasības, pārvadātājiem, kas sniedz komercpārvadājumus ar vieglo automobili, jāaprīko transportlīdzeklis ar informāciju par mobilās lietotnes vai tīmekļvietnes pakalpojuma sniedzēju, piemēram, *izmantojot uzlīmes*.
* Normatīvajos aktos nav noteikts konkrēts uzlīmes veids, krāsa vai izmērs, līdz ar to pārvadātājam ir tiesības izvēlēties atbilstošu formu, kādā šī informācija tiek norādīta.
* Konkrētajā gadījumā prasība ir izpildīta, jo uz abām priekšējām durvīm ir uzlīmēta Bolt mobilās lietotnes uzlīme, kas ir redzama arī Kontroles dienesta uzņemtajās fotogrāfijās.
* Iesaku kā pierādījumu pievienot jebkādu pavadzīmi vai citu dokumentu, kas apliecina Bolt uzlīmes uzlīmēšanu konkrētajam auto. 

Nobeigumā norādīt: 

# Autoparks nepiekrīt apgalvojumam, ka uz automobiļa durvīm nav norādīta tīmekļvietnes vai mobilās lietotnes pakalpojuma informācija.
# Autoparks atzīst un nožēlo pārkāpumu daļā, ka pārvadātāja informāciju nav iespējams nolasīt uz durvīm. Pārvadātājs informē, ka ir sācis rīkoties pārkāpuma novēršanai un apņemas nepieļaut līdzīga pārkāpuma atkārtošanos nākotnē.

Pamatojoties uz iepriekš minēto, autoparks lūdz kontroles dienestu *piemērot brīdinājumu kā sodu.*

Autopārvadājumu likuma 57. panta otrā daļa paredz, ka brīdinājumu vai naudas sodu (iestāde var izvēlēties, kuru no abiem soda veidiem piemērot) var piemērot gan autovadītājam, gan pārvadātājam. Šis lēmums attiecināms tieši uz pārvadātāju, taču arī autovadītājam var tikt piemērots sods.

I went through all the documents and below is the list of all the metrics that we currently have under merchant churn umbrella 

* *PoP Merchant Churn Count* - Number of providers who were NOT active in the reporting period, but were active in the previous reporting period 
* *PoP Merchant Churn Rate* - Number of providers who were NOT active in the reporting period, but were active in the previous reporting period as a proportion of the total number of providers active in the previous reporting period
* *28-Day Rolling PoP Merchant Churn Rate* - The 28-Day Rolling Merchant Churn Rate is the percentage of providers who were active in one 28-day period but completely inactive in the next 28-day period. We calculate it by dividing the number of providers who were active in the previous 28-day period but showed zero activity in the current 28-day period, by the total number of providers who were active in the previous 28-day period.
* *PoP Resurrected Merchant Count* - Providers who were considered churned in the previous reporting period but have returned to the platform in the reporting period
* *ELC Churn* - ELC (Early Life Cycle) churn refers to providers who stop using our platform during their first 30 days. Specifically, these are providers whose total lifetime on our platform was 29 days or less before they became inactive.
* *Pre live churn %* - Total Number of Merchant that we onboard that never went live / Total Number of Merchants we onboard
* *Merchant Churn (Provider Level)* - A provider is considered churned if they haven't shown any activity for at least 28 days. Importantly, we wait a full 28 days to confirm this inactivity before applying the 'churned' label. Once confirmed, we mark the customer's last active day as the beginning of their churn period.
* *Resurrect Merchant (Provider Level)* - A provider is considered resurrected on a given day if they were previously churned and have now returned to active status.

Hi team, 

The users are able to pay with expired cards. This happens due to a feature called account updater. 

The *Account Updater* card feature is a service used primarily by *merchants* and *payment processors* to automatically update stored card information when a customer’s card details change. It helps reduce *transaction declines* and *customer friction* in recurring or subscription billing scenarios.

Every card has a network token. Even if the card expires the token remains the same. If a customer is trying to use an expired card then we are able to charge their account through the token. 

Let me know if you have questions. 

Cheers, 
Marten

# *QUESTION:* can you please confirm that you will have clear rules to establish fraud? Are you able to share the rules or documented instructions in Beehive?

Rules - 

* Intentional overcharges (Driver fraudulently asked for more money) 
* Ignoring ride discounts for the full fare on cash trips and 
* Overcharges from using a longer route.

For cash-paid trips without electronic payment (mobile money or bank transfers), the driver’s history of repeated offenses (comments left on their profile) would warrant a deduction on the third instance. However, electronic payment proof from the rider justifies immediate deduction, even on the first report.



# *QUESTION:* Do you have any concerns with this or is this not realistic in your opinion?

This is already being done via in-app notification/pop-up and comes with the particular order details. This will continue and not change.



# *QUESTION:* do you consider an option for drivers to dispute with Bolt to be possible? If yes, how do you envision this procedure to apply?

Since drivers are notified about the deduction, they are at liberty to dispute the deduction and it will be addressed. Like all other driver issues, this will be addressed on Beehive and DEC.



# *Third parties:* are any third parties involved for the purpose of the deductions feature?

No, third parties will not be involved in this process or the purpose of it. Deductions will be done on Beehive.

# *Retention policy:* how long do you need to store the deduction-related data? Do you prefer any particular retention period to apply?

Deduction-related data should be retained for the same duration as driver balance data, which is permanent, given the critical link between the feature and the balance history.

# *Location:* can you confirm that the feature will go live only in Ghana? Do we have any plans to roll it out globally?

This deduction feature is currently specific to Ghana and Nigeria. Future adoption in other markets will depend on their strategies and priorities.

* Ou of the markets that are currently not signed off by Commerce Compliance, high interest markets are:
** Non-EU: AZ, TN
** EU: NL, BE, CH, FI, DE

As a reminder:

* Framework for Commerce Compliance sign-offs to cash cancellation fee collection is described in FinReg Playbook section “[+(Cash) ride cancellation fee+|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1AZ6R3pQcPhwHNTbSdXytaZeG3T1CvIgO0N50WP1DcK4/edit?tab=t.0#heading=h.k0gpy3logv2y]”.

As regards the above markets:

* AZ: Has EU-like regulation and is subject to same restrictions as EU: 1) cash cancellation fee collection via in-app payment is ok; 2) cash cancellation fee collection by other drivers/fleet is no-go.
* TN: Does not have EU-like restrictions. So, in principle both ways for cash cancellation fee collection are ok. However, my latest understanding was that TN went lightweight - please check that.
* EU:  Status is same, 1) cash cancellation fee collection via in-app payment is ok; 2) cash cancellation fee collection by other drivers/fleet is no-go. Do note that the planned localisation in NL will likely increase FinReg risks, because payments become handled by the local entity, which the financial regulators pay more attention to than cross-border payment activity. 
* FinReg team has currently no resource to launch additional discussions with EU or AZ regulators in this matter to try to seek their approval to item 2).

* Ads & Monetised activities in the app (invoiced to suppliers) is a similar to promotional activities

* *Budgeting and ROI:* The way you budget for and calculate return on investment is different. Ad spend is often directly tied to performance metrics ( return on ad spend). Promotional spend might have a less direct, harder-to-measure ROI, focusing more on sales uplift, engagement and future sales.
* In essence, Ads & Monetisation is primarily about how a platform/publisher makes money from its audience or advertisers, while Promotional Activities are about how a brand markets itself to its audience to achieve various business objectives, often by providing value (sales uplift) or creating buzz (contests, competition). *While we are using ads* *_to promote_* *a promotional activity, they are distinct functions serving different immediate purposes.*

# *O registo do veículo é aceite sem o nome da empresa operadora de TVDE constar no DUA e sem contrato de comodato?*

Não. A plataforma apenas aceita o registo de veículos quando está presente *uma das seguintes condições*:

* O nome da empresa operadora de TVDE consta do DUA; ou
* Existe um *contrato de comodato* válido entre o titular do veículo e a entidade operadora.



# *É aceite o registo de veículos cujos documentos estejam apenas em nome de um cidadão singular, que não seja o motorista registado na plataforma?*

Sim, desde que exista *um vínculo documental que comprove a relação entre o titular do veículo e a frota*, como por exemplo um contrato de comodato.



# *Os motoristas em nome individual, sem vínculo escrito (contrato) com a empresa operadora licenciada para TVDE, são obrigados a emitir recibos?*

Sim, os motoristas que operam em nome individual estão legalmente obrigados a emitir recibos pelos serviços prestados.

Contudo, importa referir que a *Bolt não tem qualquer intervenção na relação contratual ou fiscal entre os motoristas e as empresas operadoras (frotas)*.

A responsabilidade pelo enquadramento legal e fiscal dessa relação recai sobre a empresa operadora com a qual o motorista colabora.

Hello! Below is the proposed response, based on the information provided. Thank you

----

Exmo (a). Senhor (a)
Diretor(a) da Direção de Supervisão da Autoridade da Mobilidade e dos Transportes (AMT)

Na sequência do pedido de esclarecimentos remetido a propósito da inscrição de veículos TVDE na plataforma Bolt, vem a Bolt prestar as seguintes respostas às questões remetidas:

# +O registo do veículo é aceite sem o nome da empresa operadora de TVDE constar no DUA e sem contrato de comodato?+

Não. A plataforma apenas aceita o registo de veículos quando está presente uma das seguintes condições:

* O nome da empresa Operadora de TVDE consta do DUA; ou
* Existe um contrato de comodato válido entre o titular do veículo e a entidade Operadora de TVDE.

# +É aceite o registo de veículos cujos documentos estejam apenas em nome de um cidadão singular, que não seja o motorista registado na plataforma?+

Os documentos do veículo devem estar vinculados ao Operador TVDE, e não ao motorista, uma vez que, habitualmente, é o Operador TVDE o proprietário do veículo, e não o motorista. O nome do motorista apenas consta dos documentos relativos ao veículo, se este for o seu respetivo proprietário.

Neste sentido, apenas é aceite o registo de veículos de cujo documento conste o nome de uma pessoa singular que não seja o motorista registado na plataforma se existir um vínculo documental que comprove a relação entre o titular do veículo e o Operador TVDE, como por exemplo um contrato de comodato.

# +Os motoristas em nome individual, sem vínculo escrito (contrato) com a empresa operadora licenciada para TVDE, sem contrato de trabalho e ou de prestação de serviços, são obrigados a emitir recibos?+

Nos termos da Lei n.º 45/2018, de 10 de Agosto, os motoristas de TVDE prestam serviço ao Operador TVDE.

De acordo com os termos e condições aplicáveis (disponíveis em [https://bolt.eu/pt-pt/legal/tnc-tvde-operators/?category=rides),|https://bolt.eu/pt-pt/legal/tnc-tvde-operators/?category=rides),|smart-link]  o preço da viagem é pago pelo utilizador ao Operador TVDE, pela prestação dos serviços de transporte, sendo que o Operador TVDE autoriza a Bolt, enquanto agente comercial, a receber o preço da viagem e a remeter os fundos aplicáveis ao Operador TVDE.

Nestes termos, os motoristas sem vínculo contratual com o Operador TVDE estão obrigados a emitir um recibo pelos serviços prestados ao Operador TVDE, como qualquer prestador de serviços em nome individual.

Contudo, salienta-se que a Bolt não tem qualquer intervenção na relação contratual que titula a prestação de serviços do motorista ao Operador TVDE, nem no enquadramento fiscal da mesma. A responsabilidade pelo enquadramento contratual e fiscal dessa relação recai sobre o Operador TVDE, à qual o motorista presta serviços, e sobre o respetivo motorista.

A Bolt encontra-se ao dispor para qualquer colaboração ou esclarecimentos adicionais necessários.

Atentamente,

What have we in {{ng_delivery_spark.dim_provider}} 👀 

* {{merchant_type_2}} is null on 94% of active providers, 23% of fraud is when it is not null
* better than tags for electronics, worse for alcohol 

*query*

{code:sql}SELECT 
    alco_merchant_type,
    ROUND(SUM(user_price_eur)) AS price,
    ROUND(SUM(potential_fraud_loss_eur)) AS pot,
    ROUND(SUM(reporting_fraud_loss_eur)) AS rep,
    ROUND(SUM(potential_fraud_loss_eur) / SUM(user_price_eur), 3) AS pot_to_price
FROM (
    SELECT
        dod.provider_id, 
        -- case when pr.provider_tags_list like '%Electronics%' then true else false end as electronics_tag,
        -- case when pr.merchant_type_2 = 'Electronics Stores' then true else false end as electronics_merchant_type,
        case when pr.provider_tags_list like '%Wine%' or pr.provider_tags_list like '%Beer%' or pr.provider_tags_list like '%Alcohol%'  
          then true else false end as alco_tag,
        case when pr.merchant_type_2 = 'Alcohol Stores' then true else false end as alco_merchant_type,
        dod.provider_name,
        dod.order_id,
        etl.reporting_fraud_loss_eur, 
        etl.potential_fraud_loss_eur, 
        etl.user_price_eur
    FROM 
        ng_delivery_spark.dim_order_delivery AS dod
    LEFT JOIN 
        ng_public_spark.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl
        ON dod.order_id = etl.order_id
        AND etl.created_date BETWEEN date_add(current_date, -150) AND date_add(current_date, -60)
        AND etl.order_type = 'food_delivery'
    LEFT JOIN ng_delivery_spark.dim_provider AS pr
      ON pr.provider_id=dod.provider_id 
    WHERE 
        dod.order_created_date BETWEEN date_add(current_date, -150) AND date_add(current_date, -60)
        AND dod.order_state = 'delivered'
        AND dod.payment_method_type IN ('processout', 'card')
)
GROUP BY 1

!EasyDMARC – all our Braze platform dedicated IPs blacklist monitoring view.png|width=2046,height=936,alt="EasyDMARC – all our Braze platform dedicated IPs blacklist monitoring view.png"!



!EasyDMARC dashboard – email compliance view.png|width=2940,height=1450,alt="EasyDMARC dashboard – email compliance view.png"!

*How this platform works*

We as a brand send emails to users who have their email addresses with various providers (Gmail, Yahoo, Outlook, Apple and so on).

Once our sent email is received by the provider, they then send back to us anonymised report about technical compliance (SPF, DKIM, DMARC alignment) of that email and some information where did the sent email end up (spam, was not delivered at all, or was successfully delivered based on technical setup). This platform basically gathers all those reports from various mailbox providers in a unified dashboard.
There’s no customer email addresses anywhere in this tool since the reports are already anonymised by the mailbox providers.

We also use this platform to add our Braze tool dedicated IP addresses so that they are monitored and we would get alerts if any of the IP addresses are blacklisted somewhere and we need to take actions to fix it.

*What the platform “sees”*
Our total aggregated sent email volume from [bolt.eu|http://bolt.eu] domain and its subdomains.

Tools that we use to send those emails (Google workspace, Braze, Sendgrid, Amazon SES, etc. – as sending sources)

If that sent volume is compliant from technical standpoint (SPF, DKIM, DMARC DNS records and technical setup)

*What the platform “doesn’t see”*
Who is the end recipient of the emails that we send. They only know for example that we sent an email to Gmail as a provider (because Gmail sent back anonymised report back to us), but there is no information anywhere to what exact email address recipient of gmail was the email sent at the end.

Hope this helps a bit, and if anything, we can setup a quick call to go over this if needed 🙏

*** try to take out the counterfactual
*** compare alphas (should be different) - az.plot_trace()
* If alphas do not change in specification w/o counterfactual => we might be having error in modelling
* If alphas  change in specification w/o counterfactual => seasonality might just be too weak“
